statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 5 (low) remains far below the block threshold: NQ trades 29,505.25 on an 08:15 UTC quote, above Friday's 29,491.75 settlement, with the 29,274.75 overnight low intact for roughly eight hours and the whole geopolitical decline still retraced. Stress rises to 39 (moderate) because the crude risk premium has turned back up, Brent to $90.50 and WTI to $85.60, VIX to 15.19, on the final August session of a month-end rebalancing day that opens payrolls week.
recommendation: Conditions map to EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers 13:30-14:30 UTC, where the U.S. cash open on the final August session meets month-end rebalancing, the Dallas Fed Manufacturing print and the first deep-liquidity pricing of the weekend Larak Island exchange. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 holds its full overnight retracement while the crude risk premium rebuilds, leaving month-end rebalancing and the unresolved September rate-hike debate as the day's live checkpoints
body:
The retracement is still holding. The Nasdaq-100 September contract trades 29,505.25, up 13.50 points or 0.05% against Friday's 29,491.75 settlement, inside an unchanged overnight range of 29,274.75 to 29,545.50 on a quote timestamped 08:15 UTC. The 29,274.75 low was printed around the 00:00 UTC hour after the United States struck two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island and Iran's Revolutionary Guards answered with missiles at American bases in Jordan, eight of which Jordanian air defences intercepted without casualties. That low has now stood for roughly eight hours, neither extreme of the range has been tested this hour, and the entire 236-point decline remains retraced. A completed retracement that then holds is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement path the tail measure is built to detect, so Tail stays at 5. S&P 500 futures at 7,710.75, down 0.15%, and Dow futures down 0.17% show the same broadly flat shape with a small negative tilt.

The change this hour is in crude, and it runs the other way from last hour. Brent trades $90.50, up 2.72%, and WTI $85.60, up 2.64%, both above the $89.60 and $84.66 readings of an hour earlier. The Hormuz risk premium is rebuilding rather than decaying. VIX has moved with it, printing 15.19 at 08:11 UTC against Friday's 14.43 close, a 5.3% rise that is still a low absolute level. Energy firming while equity futures sit flat is a divergence, and divergence of that kind belongs in Stress rather than Tail: there is no persistent directional structure in NQ to amplify.

The weekend also produced a claim that Kharg Island, which handles roughly 90% of Iran's crude exports, had been hit. Verification places that as an AI-generated social-media post from President Trump with no evidence of an actual strike, alongside a statement from President Pezeshkian that Tehran is not seeking war. It is scored as headline risk, not as confirmed supply loss. Reporting adds that further U.S. secondary sanctions on Iran's trading partners are expected on a rolling weekly basis, which keeps an unscheduled headline channel open through the session.

The rates backdrop is unchanged and remains a substantial Stress contributor. After Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole remarks the September meeting has repriced from roughly 70% odds of a hold to something close to a coin flip on a quarter-point increase, with prediction-market and futures venues spanning the high forties to around 60%. The Federal Reserve H.15 release shows the 2-year at 4.20% and the 10-year at 4.67%, and Treasury futures are modestly bid across the curve.

Today is the final August session. The Dow is up 2.1% for the month and on course for a fifth consecutive monthly advance, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite are up about 3% and 4% for their first monthly gains since May. That makes month-end rebalancing a mechanical flow concentrated into the 13:30 UTC open and the 20:00 UTC close, which is why the danger window is drawn narrowly around the open rather than across the session. The only scheduled U.S. release is the Dallas Fed Manufacturing Index at 14:30 UTC. The week's substance arrives later: ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS on Tuesday, ADP and the Beige Book on Wednesday, ISM Services on Thursday, and August payrolls on Friday, with Broadcom reporting after Wednesday's close.

The shared Finviz cross-asset context collected at 07:43 UTC is fresh and complete this hour, and it is used as delayed supporting context only. It shows every one of the seven tracked semiconductors lower in the latest session, a mean of -2.49% with NVDA at -4.57% and ARM at -6.33%, against megacaps split five positive to three and sector performance divided between Technology at -1.41% and Communication Services and Consumer Cyclical both up more than 1.3%. Conflicting breadth of that kind reduces directional conviction rather than confirming a trend, which supports the mixed dominant mode and the higher Stress reading without lifting Tail. Stress therefore rises to 39 while Tail holds at 5. Confidence is 88, supported by a live NQ quote, S&P futures, both crude benchmarks, a live VIX print, the H.15 curve, a verified seven-day calendar, verified reporting on the weekend escalation and fresh complete Finviz context.

lookbackSummary: Across the previous 24 hourly assessments Tail ran at 5 through Friday's aftermath and the quiet Sunday session, stepped to 9 in the 22:00 UTC hour and peaked at 15 in the 00:00 UTC hour as the Larak Island exchange drove NQ to 29,274.75. Stress rose in parallel from 26 to a high of 44. Every hour since has walked Tail back - 13, 11, 10, 10, 8, 6, 5 - as the overnight low held and the decline was fully retraced, while dominant mode moved from normal through trend-down to mixed. No hour reached the watch threshold and the mapped state stayed EA_ON throughout.
outlookSummary: The base case over the next 24 hours is continued two-way trade with Tail held in the 5 to 10 band and no hour reaching the 20 watch threshold, so the mapped state remains EA_ON across the window. Two narrow checkpoints carry the elevated conditional readings: the 13:30 UTC cash open on the final August session, where month-end rebalancing meets the Dallas Fed print and the first deep-liquidity pricing of the weekend escalation, and the 19:00 UTC hour into the 20:00 UTC close where that rebalancing settles. Stress peaks near 46 around the open and decays to the mid-30s overnight, while Confidence falls from 88 to 58 with distance from the 08:15 UTC live quote.
